note: Edge-function .from() names absent from BOTH the Drizzle definitions in shared/ and the CREATE TABLE/VIEW statements in drizzle/. Absence here is a QUESTION, not a defect: COP-M00 counted 107 tables that exist live and are in no Drizzle schema, created by db:push before the migration workflow landed. database-schema-report.json cannot settle it either - it is a June snapshot that predates web_forms, among others.
contract: WF-G-02: `allowed` is an allow-list, not a ratchet. Every entry must carry a non-empty `reason` and the `story` that owns the decision, and the guard fails without them. --update-baseline PRUNES ONLY - it never adds an entry, so a new undeclared relation cannot enter without somebody writing down why it is acceptable.
unreviewedNote: The pre-existing entries, carried over verbatim when the allow-list contract landed. They are NOT justified and NOT accepted - they are a triage queue, shrink-only. Do not add to it. Writing 73 plausible-sounding reasons in one pass would have been the same fabrication this guard exists to catch, so only the entries with an identified owning story were promoted. To triage one: run --list (it flags every file that discards the PostgREST error, which is how a missing relation renders as an empty list at 200), find or file the story that owns the feature, then move the entry into `allowed` with a reason.

sales_handoffs.reason: No schema, no migration. The handoff model that DOES exist is shared/sales-handoff-schema.ts (sales_handoff_checklists, handoff_task_templates, handoff_tasks, implementation_projects), served by server/routes-sales-handoff.ts, which has no caller; this edge function is in docs/unreferenced-edge-fns-baseline.json, so nothing reaches either. Two models, neither wired. WF-C-06 decides which survives and builds the operations queue on it; creating sales_handoffs to satisfy this guard would entrench the wrong one.

work_orders.reason: No schema, no migration. work-orders/ and service-contracts/ are both unreferenced by every client tree, but technician-management IS reachable and its GET /:id/schedule does `const { data: schedule } = await query` then `schedule || []` - the error is discarded, so a technician's schedule is a permanent empty list at 200 rather than an error. That handler is the live half and is what WF-V-07 owns.

appointments.reason: No schema, no migration; the nearest declared relation is customer_maintenance_appointments, which is the customer portal's, not this. scheduling/ is unreferenced, but today-dashboard IS reachable (the iOS app calls it, APIEndpoint.swift) and discards the error the same way, so today's appointments are permanently empty there. WF-L-06 owns the delivery/installation scheduling model these two would sit on; it names delivery_schedules and installation_schedules, so the table this becomes is part of that decision.

lead_routing_rules.reason: No schema, no migration, no RLS file. This is the one entry of the six that is already handled honestly: EDGE-002g removed the two fabricated sample rules this function used to return at 200 and the rule endpoints now answer 503 ROUTING_RULES_UNAVAILABLE, so an admin is told the feature is unavailable rather than shown rules that do not exist. WF-S-02 creates the table.

maintenance_schedules.reason: No schema, no migration - and maintenance_records beside it is in the same state. server/routes-preventive-maintenance.ts serves dev from hard-coded fixtures (its own comments say so), so the two hosts disagree about whether preventive maintenance exists at all. WF-V-04 deletes the fixtures and decides the schema; that decision, not this guard, is what the table shape should follow.

purchase_order_line_items.reason: No schema, no migration, and unlike the rest of these the correct relation is already known: purchase_order_items, declared in BOTH shared/schema.ts and shared/equipment-schema.ts with different shapes (which is check:dup-tables' half of the story). 16 references in purchase-orders/index.ts point at the wrong name. WF-P-01 repoints them and resolves the duplicate declaration; this entry exists so the guard does not report the same defect twice.
